title: Where Newton's method sends each point
lede: Each pixel is a starting guess for Newton's method on a cubic with three roots. It takes the color of the root it reaches; darker means more steps. Drag the roots, or change the number of steps shown.
notice: With few iterations most of the plane is still unsettled. As the count rises, the three basins fill in around the roots.
The border between basins is never a clean line: near it, tiny changes in the start send the iteration to different roots.
Points close to a root settle in a step or two. Points near where the derivative is zero get thrown far away first.
hint: Drag a root circle, or slide the iteration count from 1 to 30.
